original.target_description: Study 1 Brand Evaluation Index: main brand-name effect; omnibus and timing-conditional main effects are candidates.

n.sample_role: Participants contributing to target Study 1 ANCOVA; analytic count not explicitly established. Reported whole-study participation count: 126 undergraduates.
n.exclusions: No explicit target-model exclusions, missing-data counts, or final condition-group counts reported in inspected Study 1 Method/Results.
n.location: Manuscript pp. 9, 12–13, Study 1 Procedure and Brand Evaluation Index
n.quote:
One hundred and twenty-six undergraduate students in a large northeastern

university participated in the study for partial course credit. ... A 2 x 2 x 2 ANCOVA on the Brand Evaluation Index revealed the

predicted three-way interaction (F(1,118) = 4.78, p < .05). As with the Attribute Perception

Index, the main effect of brand name was significant (F(1,118) = 9.39, p < .01); no other effect

was significant. ... When the diagnostic information was provided

simultaneously with the sound symbolism of the brand names, the main effect of sound

symbolism was significant (F(1,121) = 9.29, p < .01), such that Frosh (M = 4.84) was rated

higher than Frish (M = 4.00) on the Brand Evaluation Index regardless of whether the name was

described as true or test, supporting hypothesis 1 and hypothesis 3b.

notes: Identity: supplied canonical text has the matching title A Sound Idea: Phonetic Effects of Brand Names on Consumer Judgments and authors Eric Yorkston and Geeta Menon; its provenance header names DOI 10.1086/383422 and an NYU author-hosted PDF URL. It is a full primary research manuscript (methods, results, references, figures), dated 02/25/03, rather than the typeset 2004 JCR article. The header DOI alone is not independent bibliographic verification; version/pagination differences remain. No PDF was supplied. Text printed pp. 9–13 correspond to the Study 1 material; supplied published-page locators cannot be checked directly. Study 1 reports 126 undergraduate participants in Procedure, but does not explicitly identify a final analytic sample or final mutually exclusive group counts for these ANCOVAs. Exclusions/missingness are not documented in the inspected Study 1 Method and Results. Analytic N cannot be established from participation alone; no N was inferred from denominator degrees of freedom. No arithmetic derivation was made. Only assigned n_o is assessed; other side/fields are unassigned placeholders. Candidates: omnibus F(1,118) = 9.39, p < .01; conditional F(1,121) = 10.83, p < .01 (p. 12); conditional F(1,121) = 9.29, p < .01 (p. 13). Timing labels in the manuscript brand-evaluation simple-effects prose appear reversed relative to its hypothesis interpretation; retained without correction.
